title: Single-Threaded Execution Check
description: Predict sync vs scheduled setTimeout order on one thread.

questions.explanation: Synchronous logs run to completion first (`A`, then `C`). `setTimeout` only schedules `B` for later, even with delay `0`.

questions.prompt: What does `setTimeout(fn, 0)` do on the current synchronous pass?

options.text: Runs `fn` immediately before the next line
Pauses the thread for 0 ms then runs `fn`
Schedules `fn` for later; sync code keeps running
Cancels all other timers and runs `fn`

questions.explanation: `setTimeout` schedules a callback. It does not pause the current line or jump ahead of remaining sync work.

options.text: Because `4` is scheduled as a microtask
Because sync code finishes before any timer callback runs
Because nested timers run before outer timers
Because `console.log(4)` has higher priority than timers

questions.explanation: `1` and `4` are synchronous. The outer timer callback (which prints `2`) cannot run until the call stack is clear of that sync pass.

questions.prompt: When is the inner `setTimeout` that prints `3` scheduled in the nested example?

options.text: At the same time as the outer timer is registered
Only after the outer timer callback starts running

questions.explanation: The inner timer is registered inside the outer callback, so it cannot be scheduled until that callback runs after sync work finishes.
